chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh narrated to me from his uncle, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ibn Faddal, from Sa'id ibn Ghazwan, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his father, from his ancestors, from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The devil remains fearful of the son of Adam, retreating from him, as long as he offers the five prayers at their proper times. But when he neglects them, the devil becomes bold against him and leads him into major sins.'
ai.seo_question: How does neglecting the five daily prayers affect Satan's influence over a person?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A'mal* highlights the psychological and spiritual mechanism of *al-ha'ib* (fearfulness) and *al-daa'ir* (retreat) of Satan, illustrating how consistent *Salat* acts as a divine shield. In Shia tradition, this emphasizes that the five daily prayers are not merely ritual obligations but active defenses against the accuser's influence, where neglect invites a cumulative escalation into major sins (*al-'aza'im*).
